`CLAUDE.md`; the design lives in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`.

Status values: `todo | in_progress | done | blocked`.

### Gates and what each fails without

In milestone 0 four gates guarded artefacts that did not exist yet, and passed while
there was nothing to check. Every subject exists now, and none of them may pass without
it (verified against the scripts on 2026-10-12; the Decisions row of that date says what
was still left over and was fixed):

| Gate | Fails without |
|---|---|
| `make contracts` | generated code in sync; `api/openapi/admin.yaml`; at least one document in `api/asyncapi`; `api/proto` that lints and is formatted; a reference commit (`CONTRACT_BASE`, or `HEAD`) that exists **and holds** the management API and the node RPC to compare with - a reference without them fails, it is no longer "nothing to compare with" |
| `make s3-compat` | `test/s3compat/baseline.txt` with at least one test recorded; a suite that builds and runs; every recorded test passing; `TestCephS3Tests` and `TestAWSCLICopyUpAndDown` in the baseline where the tools are built in |
| `make helm-lint` | `deploy/helm/cactusfs/Chart.yaml` (no "no chart yet"); an `appVersion` that is `internal/buildinfo/VERSION`; at least one value set in `ci/` and one in `ci/refused/`; every render valid, asserted, and every refusal refused for the reason it names |
| `make licences` | at least one third-party module linked on each of the six platforms; at least one production package of the console |
| `make observability-check` | the rules, their tests and the chart's copy; at least one dashboard; at least one value set in `ci/monitoring/`; the four Go tests it runs, each found by name before it is run (`go test -run` is content with a name that matches nothing) |
| `make cover`, `make fmt-check`, `make lint` | measured statements in `internal/domain` and `internal/app`; Go files to read |
| `make test-int` | black-box tests of the real binary, of a four-node cluster of product-image containers, of Vault, and of NATS JetStream with a webhook receiver (`TestBucketNotifications`, 8.2.6; the audit trail through a target, 8.2.8), and of two sites - the four-node cluster replicating to a standalone node of its own CA and key file on its network (`TestSiteReplication`, 8.1.8), which pauses that node's container (`docker pause`): with rootless Podman the engine needs cgroup v2 with the `freezer` controller delegated to the user (`cgroup.freeze` is cgroup v2's; a rootless engine on cgroup v1 cannot pause) - all real containers through testcontainers-go, each image pinned by digest; nothing stands in for any of them. `INT_RUN=<pattern>` narrows a run to the tests it matches (verbosely; it fails when none does) and `make check` refuses it |

`make up`, `make down`, `make test-chaos`, `make test-rolling` and `make test-k8s` are
implemented (3.8; 2.8 and 3.9; G.6; 7.10) and are not part of `make check`; the last three
are CI jobs of their own. `make test-rolling` fails when the test it names is not there.

Still tolerated, on purpose: `scripts/release.sh --dry-run` writes no `SHA256SUMS` when
`dist/` holds no binary and says so (inside `make check` the binaries are always built
first; `--publish` requires all six).

## Milestone 2 — Erasure coding and integrity on local drives

Done when a standalone node with four or more drives survives the loss or corruption of
up to *parity* drives without a failed read, repairs itself, and `make test-chaos` is
green.

| ID | Status | Step | Acceptance criterion | Files |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2.1 | done | Erasure domain: parameters, quorum, stripe geometry, set layout | parity 2/3/4 by set size, 1+0 below four drives; write quorum = data (+1 when data = parity); sets of 4–16 drives, equal size; property tests on the geometry | `internal/domain/erasure/` |
| 2.2 | done | Reed-Solomon codec behind `ports.ErasureCodec` | `klauspost/reedsolomon`; property test: encode → lose ≤ parity shards → decode equals original; fuzz; contract test | `internal/ports/erasure.go`, `internal/adapters/erasurecodec/` |
| 2.3 | done | Topology in metadata and striped storage | drive slots recorded through Raft and addressed by drive ID, so reordering `--data` is harmless; shards of one object never share a drive; write succeeds on a write quorum and fails below it; reads reconstruct from any *data* shards; ADR | `internal/adapters/raftmeta/`, `internal/app/storage.go`, `internal/app/topology.go`, `docs/adr/0004-erasure-and-topology.md` |
| 2.4 | done | Heal | a degraded read queues the version; healing rebuilds missing, truncated and corrupt shards from the others and verifies the object is still current; a replaced (empty) drive is adopted into its slot and refilled | `internal/app/heal.go` |
| 2.5 | done | Background scrubber | walks every object, verifies every shard block, heals what it finds; rate-limited; `--scrub-interval`; metrics | `internal/app/scrub.go`, `cmd/cactusfs/` |
| 2.6 | done | Fewer than four drives | 1+0 on one drive each, encrypted and checksummed; logs that there is no parity | `internal/domain/erasure/`, `cmd/cactusfs/` |
| 2.7 | done | Garbage collection of unreferenced shards | `ShardStore.List`; a data-ID index in the state machine; shards older than `--gc-grace` that no version refers to are removed | `internal/ports/shards.go`, `internal/adapters/disk/`, `internal/adapters/raftmeta/`, `internal/app/gc.go` |
| 2.8 | done | Chaos suite | against the built binary with six drives: corrupt shards, delete shards, wipe up to *parity* drives → every read is correct and the drives are repaired; one more than parity → reads fail, never wrong data; `make test-chaos` | `test/chaos/`, `Makefile` |

## Milestone 3 — Cluster

Design (ADR-0005): every node runs Raft — `meta` nodes as voters, the others as
non-voters — so every node holds the metadata locally. Changes are forwarded to the
leader over node RPC; reads wait for the leader's read index. Shards are reached through
`ports.ShardStore` whether the drive is local or on another node. A cluster is formed
once, from the complete list of its nodes (`--peers`); its erasure sets are planned
across nodes, racks and zones at that moment.

| ID | Status | Step | Acceptance criterion | Files |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3.1 | done | Cluster domain: nodes, roles, topology labels | `--roles` selects gateway/meta/storage/console; `region/zone/rack/host` labels; topology planned across nodes, then racks/zones; a node answers for its own drives only | `internal/domain/cluster/`, `cmd/cactusfs/` |
| 3.2 | done | Node RPC over mTLS 1.3 | gRPC contract in `api/proto/`; generated code committed; `buf lint` and `buf breaking` in `make contracts`; a remote drive passes the same `ShardStore` contract as a local one; every call passes the authorizer as a node principal | `api/proto/`, `internal/adapters/noderpc/`, `internal/adapters/nodetls/`, `buf.yaml`, `buf.gen.yaml`, `scripts/{gen,contracts}.sh`, `Dockerfile` |
| 3.3 | done | Multi-node Raft (3 or 5 voters) over mTLS | formation from identical peer lists, join, leave, leader change, linearizable reads on every node; a node never logs an entry newer than the oldest node understands (rolling upgrade N ↔ N+1 test) | `internal/adapters/raftmeta/`, `docs/adr/0005-cluster.md` |
| 3.4 | done | Distributed erasure sets | shards of one object on different nodes where the cluster allows; the tolerated number of node failures is computed and logged | `internal/domain/cluster/topology.go`, `internal/app/topology.go`, `internal/ports/drives.go` |
| 3.5 | done | Quorum write and read paths | no acknowledgement before write quorum + Raft commit; reads and writes survive nodes that are down up to parity; an unreachable drive is neither damage nor a reason to delete; read-after-write on every node | `internal/app/`, `internal/domain/errors.go` |
| 3.6 | done | Events from applied Raft entries | contract first in `api/asyncapi/events.yaml`, AsyncAPI validation in `make contracts`; in-process bus; consumers dedupe by event ID | `api/asyncapi/events.yaml`, `scripts/contracts.sh`, `internal/ports/events.go`, `internal/adapters/events/inproc/` |
| 3.7 | done | Integration tests on a real cluster | testcontainers-go: four containers of the product image form a cluster over mTLS; S3 through every node | `test/integration/` |
| 3.8 | done | Compose deployment | 4-node cluster; unchanged on `docker compose` and rootless `podman compose`; `make up/down`; `cactusfs dev-init` writes the throw-away CA, certificates and shared key file | `deploy/compose/compose.yaml`, `cmd/cactusfs/devinit.go`, `Makefile` |
| 3.9 | done | Chaos: node kill, partition, heal verification | `make test-chaos` passes: cluster scenarios next to the single-node ones | `test/chaos/` |

Out of scope for milestone 3, recorded so nobody assumes otherwise: adding storage nodes
or drives to a formed cluster (new erasure sets), starting a node with one of its drives
offline, the Vault KMS adapter (4.4 — a cluster shares a sealed key file until then, and
says so at start), an operator surface for join/leave beyond the node RPC (5.x).

## Milestone 4 — IAM

Design (ADR-0006): users belong to groups; users and groups hold roles; a role is a
named set of policies; a policy is an IAM-style JSON document. An API key belongs to a
user and may carry an inline policy that can only narrow what its owner may do. The
identity of a request - key, owner, every policy that applies - is resolved in one
consistent read at authentication and travels in the principal; the one authorizer
decides on it. Everything is replicated through Raft; every IAM change carries its
audit record in the same entry.

| ID | Status | Step | Acceptance criterion | Files |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4.1 | done | IAM domain: users, groups, roles, policies | IAM-style JSON; default deny; explicit deny wins; conditions; fuzz + property tests for policy parsing and evaluation | `internal/domain/iam/` |
| 4.2 | done | Policy-backed `ports.Authorizer` | one decision point; no authorization logic in handlers; a key never exceeds its owner; denials audited | `internal/ports/iam.go`, `internal/app/authz.go`, `internal/adapters/raftmeta/iam.go` |
| 4.3 | done | API keys | secrets envelope-encrypted through the KMS, shown once; expiry, inline policy, last-used, immediate revocation; S3 requests authenticated with them | `internal/app/iam.go`, `internal/app/identity.go`, `internal/adapters/s3api/` |
| 4.4 | done | Vault Transit KMS adapter | `--kms vault`; integration test against Vault via testcontainers | `internal/adapters/kms/vault/`, `cmd/cactusfs/` |
| 4.5 | done | Built-in roles | `cluster-admin`, `bucket-admin`, `read-write`, `read-only`, `auditor`; cannot be changed or removed | `internal/domain/iam/builtin.go` |
| 4.6 | done | Audit log | append-only, hash-chained in the replicated state; IAM mutations (atomically with the change), authentication failures, denials; audit events in the AsyncAPI contract; export as JSON lines | `internal/domain/audit/`, `internal/app/audit.go`, `internal/adapters/audit/`, `api/asyncapi/events.yaml` |
| 4.7 | done | Console users | Argon2id local accounts behind `ports.IdentityProvider`; replicated sessions, short-lived; `HttpOnly`/`Secure`/`SameSite=Strict` cookie and CSRF token helpers | `internal/app/sessions.go`, `internal/adapters/passwords/`, `internal/adapters/httpsession/` |

Out of scope for milestone 4: the HTTP surface for managing IAM (admin API, milestone
5 - until then IAM is reachable through the use cases only), OIDC, SSE-KMS/SSE-C,
bucket policies (6.x).

## Milestone 6 — S3 depth

Built in this order; each step lands green on its own. Designs: ADR-0008 (versions in
the metadata state, entry schema v2), ADR-0009 (Object Lock and the clock that decides),
ADR-0010 (key hierarchy for multipart, SSE-KMS, SSE-C), ADR-0011 (resource policies,
anonymous access, CORS preflight), ADR-0012 (multipart uploads), ADR-0013 (lifecycle). `make test-chaos` before
every commit that touches the write path or the state machine.

| Step | Status | What | Acceptance criterion | Files |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6.3 | done | Presigned URLs and signed streaming SigV4 | AWS documentation vectors verify; SDK presigner in the compat suite; fuzz tests | `internal/adapters/s3api/{sigv4,chunked,payload,handler}.go` |
| 6.0 | done | Foundations (entry schema 2 and the leader's time; strict XML decoder, with 6.2; extent refactor of shard storage, with 6.1; the routing table was not built - see Decisions) | entry schema v2 gate (`MetadataVersion` 2, state schema 2 written by the first v2 entry); leader-stamped time `entry.At` with a high-water mark in the state; `applyEntry` receives the Raft index; `object.Extent` refactor of shard storage; per-operation allow-lists of query parameters in the S3 router (kept as a switch, not the table first planned); strict bounded XML decoder | `internal/adapters/raftmeta/{entry,fsm,store}.go`, `internal/app/storage.go`, `internal/domain/object/`, `internal/adapters/s3api/` |

## Goals B, C, D — one change of schema (Albie, 2026-10-11)

B: who uploaded an object, when, how often it was downloaded and by whom. C: search, sub-buckets.
D: tags in the console, rules for tags, a catalogue of tags. Planned with the `planner` subagent
(twice). All three change replicated state, so they share ONE rise of the entry schema, to 3, one
fixture written by the schema-2 binary, and one rolling-upgrade test. Order: S.1, S.2, the domain
steps (B.1, C.1, D.1), S.3, S.4, then B, C, D. `make test-chaos` before S.3, S.4, B.3, C.7, D.5 are
done (D.5 is D's four-node step; a "D.7" named here first was never planned).

## Milestone 8 — Hybrid

Planned with the `planner` subagent on 2026-10-12. Three sub-milestones, each green and
reported on its own, on ONE rise of the entry and state schema, to 5 (ADR-0023), as schema 3
was for goals B-D: 8.0 (the fixture, the ADRs, every contract, the whole state machine, the
rolling upgrade, targets and the delivery worker), then 8A quotas (8.3.x), 8B notifications
(8.2.x), 8C replication (8.1.x), then 8.9. Designs: ADR-0023 (schema 5, usage counters,
outbox, targets, egress), ADR-0024 (quotas), ADR-0025 (notifications, audit export),
ADR-0026 (replication and the conflict rule).

Order: 8.0.1 first, from a clean `git worktree` of 84334a7, before any schema-5 code. Then
8.0.2, 8.0.3, 8.0.4, 8.0.5, 8.0.6, 8.0.7 to 8.0.9 in that order (one package), 8.0.10, 8.0.11.
Beside 8.0.6 to 8.0.11 (other files): 8.0.12. Then 8.0.13, 8.0.14. After 8.0: 8A and 8B side
by side except the steps that touch `cmd/cactusfs/node.go`, `internal/adapters/telemetry/` and
`cmd/cactusfs/settings.go` (8.3.3, 8.2.5, 8.1.7: one at a time). 8.1.1 and 8.1.2 may run
beside 8B; 8.1.4 onward after 8.2.5. `make test-chaos` before 8.0.7, 8.0.8, 8.0.9, 8.0.10,
8.3.2, 8.3.4, 8.1.1, 8.1.9 and 8.9 are done; `make test-rolling` at 8.0.11 and 8.9;
`make test-k8s` at 8.2.9 and 8.9. New container tests are in package `test/integration`,
never `t.Parallel`, one cluster a test file; the notification and replication tests add at
most two small containers (NATS, a receiver) or one standalone node to a four-node cluster.

**8.0.14 as written (2026-11-15; `done` - reviewed, the review's findings fixed: a loop waits while its node does not lead instead of ending, a run whose target is gone is forgotten so a target made again under its name gets a loop, a failed acknowledgement holds the loop and is retried with `Backoff` so at most one batch is unacknowledged, one refresh at a time, `quota` stalls a target, the egress span ends when the body is closed; rows 8.2.5 and 8.1.4 now require the egress wiring. `make check` green on linux amd64 (`internal/domain` 96.9 %, `internal/app` 93.2 %, s3-compat 66/66), `make test-chaos` green).** No change of the contracts (`NodeService.DeliveryStatus`, `TargetDelivery` and `GET /targets/{name}/status` were complete since 8.0.3: nothing regenerated, `buf breaking` and `oasdiff` untouched), of the entry schema or of anything on disk. **The worker** (`internal/app/delivery.go`): `app.Deliverer` (`Deliver(ctx, target, item) (object.ReplicationStatus, error)`, and `DelivererFunc`), `app.DeliveryWorker` with `Run`, `DeliveryStatus` (it is the `ports.DeliveryStatusReader` of the node that leads; elsewhere `ErrNotLeader`) and `Summary` (for the gauges). `Run` asks `Active` every second; on coming to lead it starts a session that reads `ListTargets` and `OutboxCursors` at once and every 5 s and keeps one loop a target, from the cursor's `Acked`; on losing the lead it cancels the session and waits for its loops, forgetting every status. A loop reads `ReadOutbox(target, read, 100)`, passes over rows of others (an empty read with `upto` beyond is acknowledged with the rest), hands each item to the `Deliverer` of its consumer kind in order, acknowledges (`AckOutbox(target, position, 0, results)`) after 100 delivered items or when a delivered item has waited `DeliveryAckInterval` (1 s), and when it has caught up. A failure that does not pass holds the item: what was delivered before is acknowledged, the loop waits `delivery.Backoff(failures, jitter)` (jitter from `Entropy`, crypto/rand on a node) and tries the same item again; `Active` is asked before every attempt, so nothing is sent once the lead is lost. A class that passes (`rejected`, `sse_c`) gives the item up, counted (`Rejected` for `rejected`; `Failed` for a `FAILED` status). Results are kept and acknowledged for a target of kind `s3` only. Every call to the metadata carries 30 s, every attempt `AttemptTimeout`. **Tests** (`internal/app/delivery_test.go`, all in `synctest` bubbles, fake outbox and target store, fake deliverer; every call is checked for a deadline and every log for the mark): `TestDeliveryWorker` (order kept over 250 rows and three acknowledgements; a failure retried with nothing behind it sent; a `rejected` item passed and counted; `auth` stalls with the cursor where it was; `timeout` retrying; rows of others passed over; replication results; a kind nothing delivers holds its target), `TestDeliveryNothingIsSentAfterTheLeadIsLost` (while items are taken and while one is retried), `TestDeliveryARestartResendsAtMostOneBatch` (a fast target: at most 100 again; a slow one: at most what a second delivered; every row delivered, in order), `TestDeliveryTellsNoErrorOrEndpoint` (the marked URL test: endpoint and error words marked, in no status, summary or log line, the classes are), `TestDeliveryStatusAndSummary`, `TestDeliveryCountsWhatWaitsBeyondTheBatch` (2 500 rows behind: pending 2 500, the oldest the first row; a deleted target loses its loop), `TestDeliveryWhenTheOutboxCannotBeRead`, `TestDeliveryWhenAnAcknowledgementFails` (and the jittered pauses within `Backoff`). **Status** (`app.TargetService.Status`, `TargetServiceConfig.Delivery`): authorized with `admin:GetTargetStatus` on `target/<name>`, the target read (404), the reader asked with a 5 s deadline (`TargetStatusTimeout`); `ErrNotSupported` gives `state: unsupported` and zeros; a deadline is `ErrUnavailable` (503); a name the leader does not know is 404; a word that is none is not shown (`TestTargetStatus`, `TestTargetsAreAuthorized` with the status row). **Node RPC**: `ServerConfig.Delivery` (nil answers UNIMPLEMENTED, as an older release); the server drops names no target can have, refuses more than 256, sends at most 256 statuses with `ShownClass`/`shownState` applied, answers an error with its codes and a fixed message (never the words of the error); `Client.DeliveryStatus(ctx, leader, targets)` maps UNIMPLEMENTED to `ErrNotSupported`, `not_leader` to `ErrUnavailable`, and takes of the answer only names asked for, valid, once, in name order, bounded, with words sanitized again. Tests: `TestDeliveryStatusIsAuthorized`, `TestDeliveryStatusOverMutualTLS` (`porttest.DeliveryStatusContract` against a real server over mutual TLS), `TestDeliveryStatusOfANodeThatDoesNotLead`, `TestDeliveryStatusTakesOnlyWhatItAskedFor` (a hostile node). **Admin API**: `GetTargetStatus` maps the use case; `TestTargetStatus` (200 to the auditor with absent times and class left out, `unsupported`, 401, 403 to `read-only`, 404, 503); the operation is out of `TestOperationsThatAreNotWrittenYet` and of the lock test's list of unwritten operations (it now answers 423 to a locked session). **Composition** (`cmd/cactusfs`): the worker is built with the decorated targets and outbox, `Active: n.meta.IsLeader`, `OnAttempt: ObserveDeliveryAttempt`, and run in the background; `nodeDelivery` gives node RPC the worker late-bound (node RPC starts before it); `leaderDelivery` is the node's `DeliveryStatusReader` - its own worker when it leads, the leader over node RPC otherwise - decorated as port `delivery_status`. `TestANodeWiresDelivery` (standalone: 503 before the worker runs, then `ok`, 404, the gauges) and `TestTargetStatusFromAnyNode` (four nodes: every node answers, only the leader exposes the gauges); the wiring test now also requires `ports.Outbox` and `ports.DeliveryStatusReader` decorated. **Telemetry**: `InstrumentOutbox` (port `outbox`), `InstrumentDeliveryStatus` (port `delivery_status`), `InstrumentEgress` (span `egress.Do`, `cactusfs_egress_refusals_total{class}`; not wired yet - no delivery adapter exists until 8B/8C, whose wiring must put the egress client behind it), `ObserveDeliveryAttempt`, `ObserveDelivery` (the four gauges through a probe as the state gauges are); tests in `telemetry/delivery_test.go`; the label allow-list of `TestMetricsCarryNoTenantData` takes `kind`, `state`, `class`.

**8.3.1 as built (2026-11-14; reviewed, 0 blocker, 0 major, 5 minor all addressed; `make check` green on the test host 2026-11-15, s3-compat 65/65, `internal/app` 93.1 %).** `app.UsageCounter` (`quota.go`): `Run` proposes at most one `WalkBucketUsage(name, 10 000, false)` every 100 ms (`UsageWalkLimit`, `UsageWalkInterval`, a `time.Ticker`) while `Active` says this node leads; a look at every bucket (`ListBuckets`, then `BucketUsages` in chunks of `MaxBucketUsages`) queues those whose record is not exact or is walking, at once on coming to lead and then every 100 intervals (10 s), whether or not buckets are queued, adding those not queued yet; the queued buckets take turns, an entry each (a bucket still walking after its entry goes to the back), until each entry leaves its record not walking. `Recount(ctx, principal, bucket)` authorizes `admin:RecountBucketUsage` on the bucket, proposes the first entry with `restart`, audits the request in the background (`Auditor.Succeeded`; `failed` with `outcome: unknown` when the entry's outcome is unknown; ADR-0024 says so), and queues the bucket for this node's counter when the walk goes on; a node that does not lead drops its queue, and the leader finds the recount at its next look. Drift (`UsageWalk.Drift`, from the counter's entry or from the recount's first) calls `OnDrift` and is logged with the bucket's name; the metric behind `OnDrift` is 8.3.3's. `ObjectService.Usage` reads `ObjectServiceConfig.Usage` (nil until 8.3.3 wires it) after the authorizer: an exact record is the answer (`Exact`, `Complete`, `Versions`, `StoredBytes`, `UploadBytes`, `QuotaBytes`), not cached; a record that is not exact, or `ErrUnavailable`, falls back to the bounded, cached walk. Tests: `TestUsageCounter` (table, in a `testing/synctest` bubble: nothing to count, an old bucket, one bucket after the other, a recount under way goes on, standby does nothing and reads nothing, below level 5, a bucket deleted meanwhile and a fault each beside a second bucket that is counted in the next interval, a faulty bucket looked at again), `TestUsageCounterTakesTurns` (two buckets interleaved, then two recounts found by the next look), `TestUsageCounterCadence`, `TestUsageCounterChangeOfLeader`, `TestUsageOfABucketOlderThanTheRecord` (250 000 keys: 25 entries walk the keys, the 26th the uploads and finishes, then `Usage` is exact and 250 000), `TestRecount` (table: one entry, the counter, drift by either, no such bucket, unavailable), `TestRecountIsAuthorized` (cluster-admin only; refusals propose nothing; both audited), `TestRecountOfUnknownOutcome`, `TestUsageFromTheRecord` (table). |

**8.3.2 as built (2026-11-15; reviewed, 0 blocker, 1 major, 4 minor all addressed; `make check` green on the test host, s3-compat 65/65, `internal/app` 93.2 %, and `make test-chaos` green).** `app.QuotaService` (`quota.go`, `NewQuotaService(QuotaServiceConfig{Buckets, Usage, Authz, Auditor, OnRefusal})`): `Get` (`admin:GetBucketQuota`; the bucket read first, so that a missing bucket is `ErrBucketNotFound` and not the zero record; answers `BucketQuota{QuotaBytes, UsedBytes, Exact}`, `UsedBytes` 0 while not exact), `Set` (`admin:PutBucketQuota`; `bucket.ValidateQuota` before anything is proposed, so 0, below nothing and above 2^62 are `ErrInvalidArgument`; the record, with `quota_bytes` in its details, goes in the entry through `SetBucketQuota`; `ErrConflict` from the store while the bucket is counted; answers the quota read back without a second authorization), `Delete` (`admin:DeleteBucketQuota`; `SetBucketQuota(0)` with its record). `Admit(ctx, bucket, declared, frees)` is the pre-check: answered from `BucketUsages` (below level 5 no record is exact, so it admits), judged by `bucket.Usage.Admits` - the rule of the store - on what the write adds less what it frees; `frees` is read only when the write would not pass without it. `ObjectService.put` (and so `Copy`) asks it after authorization and the other admission checks and before the keys are made or a shard is begun, with `replacedVersion` (the null version of the key where versions are not kept or are suspended); `uploadPart` (and so `CopyPart`) after `GetUpload`, with `replacedPart` (the part of the same number). A commit the store refuses with `ErrQuotaExceeded` has its shards removed by `write` (unchanged) and is counted through `OnRefusal`, as a pre-check refusal is; neither is audited. `ObjectServiceConfig.Quota` is nil until 8.3.3 wires it. Completion, delete, abort and tags never ask. The S3 and admin error rows were there since 8.0.4; HTTP tests added. Tests: `TestQuotaPreCheck` (22 rows over put, part, copy and part copy: over the remainder refused with no shard begun - a counting drive - nothing counted and one refusal; unknown length refused only when full; overwrite of the same size unversioned and suspended, a part in place of one of the same size, pass a full bucket; versioned overwrite refused; no quota; a bucket being counted), `TestQuotaRefusedAtCommit` (stale advice: put, put of unknown length, part, copy, part copy - shards begun, then removed, `ErrQuotaExceeded`, one refusal counted, usage unchanged), `TestQuotaNeverRefuses` (completion, marker, tags, abort, a quota below what is held, removal for good - with advice that would refuse everything: never asked), `TestQuotaAdmit` (15 rows), `TestQuotaService` (18 steps and the five records), `TestQuotaServiceFaults` (below level 5 with the metadata fake at level 4: Get, Set, Delete unavailable, nothing changed, Admit admits; no level, a level that cannot be read), `TestQuotaServiceIsAuthorized` (cluster-admin all three, auditor reads, bucket-admin and the rest nothing; denials audited, nothing changed; `Admit` writes nothing to the trail), `s3api.TestQuotaExceededOverHTTP`, `adminapi_test.TestQuotaExceededIsAProblem`. Mutations checked: no pre-check in `put` or in `uploadPart`, nothing freed by an overwrite or by a part, shards kept on a refused commit - each fails the tests.

**8.3.3 as built (2026-11-15; reviewed, 0 blocker, 0 major, 2 minor, both addressed; `make check` green on the test host, s3-compat 65/65, `internal/app` 93.2 %; `make test-chaos` and `make test-rolling` (84334a7 to this tree) green).** The contract of 8.0 is implemented as it stands; nothing in `api/openapi/admin.yaml` changed, so nothing was generated. **Admin API** (`operations.go`): `adminapi.Config` gains `Quotas *app.QuotaService` and `Counter *app.UsageCounter` (nil: 501, as `Targets`); `getBucketQuota`, `putBucketQuota`, `deleteBucketQuota` call `QuotaService.Get/Set/Delete`, `recountBucketUsage` calls `UsageCounter.Recount` and answers 202 with no body; `quota_bytes` is absent when it is 0; `getBucketUsage` maps `exact` and, when exact, `versions`, `stored_bytes`, `upload_bytes`, and `quota_bytes` when there is one. Authorization is the use cases'; errors go through `problemOf` (409 `Conflict`, 503 with `Retry-After`, 404 `NoSuchBucket`, 400 `InvalidArgument`); `Idempotency-Key` is the pipeline's, as for every bucket operation (a bucket operation is not in `askedFirstOf`: its question depends on the bucket's policy). The four rows left `TestOperationsThatAreNotWrittenYet` and the `notWritten` list of the lock test, which now holds them to 423 for a locked session. **Telemetry**: `InstrumentBucketUsage` (port `bucket_usage`, a span and the port metrics per call, no bucket in either); counters `cactusfs_quota_refusals_total` (`ObserveQuotaRefusal`, behind `QuotaServiceConfig.OnRefusal`) and `cactusfs_bucket_usage_drift_total` (`ObserveUsageDrift`, behind `UsageCounterConfig.OnDrift`); gauges `cactusfs_buckets_quota{state=set|over_90|full}` and `cactusfs_bucket_usage_counting`, read at scrape time through a probe from a `telemetry.QuotaSource` (`ObserveQuotas`), absent when it cannot say; the source (`quotaGauges`, `observe.go`) shows a summary again for `quotaGaugesReuse` (10 s) by the node's clock before reading anew (review, see below). **App**: `QuotaService.Summary(ctx)` counts the buckets with a quota, at 90 % or more of it (`used >= quota - quota/10`, 90 % rounded up, no product that wraps), at all of it or more, and being counted, from `ListBuckets` and `BucketUsages` in chunks of `MaxBucketUsages`; it authorizes nothing and names no bucket; below level 5 it wraps `ErrUnavailable`; a context that has ended stops it before the next read of records. **Wiring** (`node.go`): one decorated `BucketUsageStore` given to `QuotaService` (`Level: metadataLevel(n.meta)`, `OnRefusal`), to `UsageCounter` (`Active: n.meta.IsLeader`, `OnDrift`, run in `startBackground`) and to `ObjectServiceConfig.Usage`, with `ObjectServiceConfig.Quota` set; `quotaGauges` (`observe.go`) attached in `open`, detached in `Close`; `server.go` gives both use cases to the handler; `ports.BucketUsageStore` joins `wiredKinds`. 401 for all three without a credential; 404 for all three of no such bucket; 200 `exact: false` and 409 for a set and a removal while counted; 204 removed and removed when there is none; repeats with a key replayed; the trail: 3 set, 2 removed, 6 denials), `TestBucketUsageFromTheRecord` (versioned bucket: versions 3, stored 12, uploads 0, quota 14; `used_bytes` 12; a put past it 403 `QuotaExceeded` by the pre-check, one refusal counted, nothing stored; a bucket being counted: the walk, `exact: false`, no record fields), `TestRecountBucketUsage` (202 with no body, the repeat replayed; a bucket being counted is exact after its recount; 403 auditor and bucket-admin, 401, 404, 415 without a media type; the trail: 2 recounts, 2 denials), `TestQuotasBelowLevel5` (all four 503 with `Retry-After`; usage `exact: false`), `TestQuotasOnANodeWithoutTheUseCases` (501), `TestTheQuotaAnswerIsTheContracts` (2^62 as a JSON integer); `app_test.TestQuotaSummary` (14 rows), `TestQuotaSummaryOfManyBuckets` (10 005 buckets, two reads), `TestQuotaSummaryFaults`; `telemetry_test.TestBucketUsageIsCountedAndTraced` (the schema 5 contract through the decorator, every method counted, no bucket name recorded), `TestQuotaCountersCountWithoutNames`, the quota source in `TestStateGauges` and `TestASourceThatHangsDoesNotHoldUpTheScrape`, `TestEveryDecoratorIsMarked`, `TestArchitectureListsTheMetrics`; `main.TestANodeWiresQuotas` (the real store: set, a put past the quota refused and counted, usage exact, the gauges `set`, `over_90`, `full` at 1, recount, removal), `TestANodeCountsUsageInTheBackground` (a recount left after one entry of one record is finished by the node's background counter alone; `cactusfs_bucket_usage_counting` back to 0; deleting the `n.counter.Run` line of `startBackground` fails it - checked), `TestQuotaGaugesAreReused` (an injected clock: reused until 10 s, read anew at 10 s, a failed summary absent and not replaced by an older one, a clock that went back reads anew), `BenchmarkQuotaSummary` (the real store, `CACTUSFS_BENCH_BUCKETS`, default 10 000), `TestEveryPortIsWiredThroughItsDecorator`.

**8.3.4 as written (2026-11-15; done: `make check` green on the test host with s3-compat 66/66 and the baseline re-recorded there unchanged, and `make test-chaos` green, after the fixes of the Decisions rows of 2026-11-15; before: - none of the three can run where this was written, which has no Docker).** Tests only; no product code changed. Compiled and vetted with every tag (`go vet -tags=integration,s3compat,s3tools,chaos ./test/...`, and `integration,rollingupgrade`), `go build ./...`, `gofumpt` clean, `golangci-lint` v2.14.0 (built with go1.27.4) `0 issues` on `./test/...`, `scripts/no-bypass.sh` PASS. **`test/integration/quota_test.go`, `TestBucketQuota`** (one cluster, not parallel; `CACTUSFS_GC_INTERVAL=2s`, `CACTUSFS_GC_GRACE=1h`): an unversioned bucket made with S3 gets a quota of 10 MiB (PUT polled while 503 or 409, any other answer fails at once); 16 writers of 1 MiB, four through each node, released together: every answer is success or 403 `QuotaExceeded` (anything else fails), exactly 10 and 6, the 10 read back through another node, the 6 are 404; usage through the leader (polled at most 30 s) is exact, 10 objects, 10 versions, 10 MiB stored, 0 uploads, quota 10 MiB; `GET .../quota` through the leader `used_bytes` 10 MiB; `cactusfs_quota_refusals_total` summed over the four nodes is 6. An overwrite of a stored key with 1 MiB through another node succeeds in the full bucket (usage unchanged), a new key is refused; a multipart upload is created and its part 1 of 5 MiB refused; six objects are deleted (usage 4 MiB), part 1 is taken, part 2 of 5 MiB refused (usage 4 MiB stored + 5 MiB uploads), a put of 1 MiB "after deleting" succeeds (exactly 10 MiB), the abort gives the 5 MiB back; refusals summed are 9. A `bucket-admin` user (key made through node1) is answered 403 problem `AccessDenied` on PUT (node2) and DELETE (node3) of the quota, usage still says the quota of 10 MiB, and the trail holds a `denied` record of each (`admin:PutBucketQuota`, `admin:DeleteBucketQuota`) with that actor, key and `arn:aws:s3:::quota` (polled 1 min). Before the collector, a usage write that must be taken after a delete is sent through a node whose own copy has been polled to show the delete (part 1 through node2, the put "after deleting" through node4: the pre-check judges on the node's copy). Last, the collector (review, major 1): an orphan shard - a copy, owner and mode kept, of one of the node's shard files under a data ID no write made, in the directory its ID names - is planted on every node (11 files of 6 IDs at least), `cactusfs_gc_shards_removed_total` is read, every shard file is made older than the grace (`touch -d` in the drive volumes through `clustertest.Shell`), `cactusfs_gc_passes_total` is read; the test waits until every node counts two passes more and has removed what it held beyond the bucket's objects, then asserts exactly that many removals (1, the orphan, unless a best-effort removal had left a shard), exactly 10 shard files of 5 data IDs - the 5 objects held - and the orphan gone; what is held reads back. **`test/s3compat/suite_test.go`, `TestQuotaExceededIsNotRetried`**: a bucket with a quota of 1 KiB holding 1000 bytes; PutObject of 100 bytes and UploadPart of 100 bytes with the suite's default client, each with a per-operation HTTP client that counts requests: 403 `QuotaExceeded`, exactly one request each, the client's retryer allowing at least 2 attempts (asserted, so the test shows something); the server's `cactusfs_quota_refusals_total` rose by exactly 2; the refused key is `NotFound`. **8.2.1 as written (2026-11-15; `done` - `make check` green on linux amd64 on 2026-11-15 (`internal/app` 93.4 %, s3-compat 66/66, licences on all six targets); locally on darwin arm64 `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofumpt -l .` clean, golangci-lint v2.14.0 on `./internal/app/...` 0 issues, `go test -race -count=3 ./internal/app/` green, `internal/app` 93.4 %; reviewed, 1 blocker, 1 major, 7 minor, all addressed - see the Decisions row of 8.2.1).** No change of a contract, a port, the entry schema or anything on disk; nothing wired (8.2.5). **Use case** (`internal/app/notify.go`): `app.NotificationService` with `Get`, `Set` and `Delete` over `ports.BucketStore` (`GetBucketConfig`/`SetBucketConfig` of kind `notification`) and `ports.TargetStore`; `Get` needs `s3:GetBucketNotification`, `Set` and `Delete` `s3:PutBucketNotification` (S3 has no action of its own for removing; IAM has no `DeleteBucketNotification`), all on the bucket through the single authorizer. `Set` with no rules removes them, as an empty `NotificationConfiguration` does. Audited as the other bucket documents are - `Auditor.Succeeded` after the commit, details `rules`, `targets` (the names) or `notification: removed`, never a prefix or suffix - because `SetBucketConfig` carries no audit record and the step allows no schema change (the record is not in the entry; a node that stops in between leaves the change unaudited, as for policy, CORS and lifecycle); without an `Auditor` every change is refused with `ErrUnavailable`, as `QuotaService` does. Before anything is proposed: a rule without an ID is given `rule-<n>`, the first `n` from 1 that no rule of the document has (deterministic, so a repeated request keeps the same rules), a rule without `as` is a queue (the admin API's default), `Document()` validates, the bucket is read (`ErrBucketNotFound` before targets are judged), and every target named must exist, be a webhook or NATS server and admit the bucket - refused with `ErrInvalidArgument` in **one sentence for all three**, so that a bucket's administrator cannot tell a target that is not there from one that is closed to the bucket (stricter than the store's three messages, which are shown only when a change races one of a target); the store decides again at commit. `Get` of a document of a later release is `ErrUnavailable`, of one that does not parse `ErrIntegrity` (as tag rules). **The record**: `app.NotificationRecord(item)` builds ADR-0025's record as compact JSON (`encoding/json` of structs, fields in the ADR's order): `eventTime` is `At` in UTC with `RFC3339Nano`; `Set` returns the rules parsed back from the document, as `Get` does; `userIdentity` absent when `By` is empty; the key is `url.QueryEscape` with `%2F` put back to `/` (`app.NotificationKey`; `url.QueryUnescape` gives the key back byte for byte, invalid UTF-8 included); `size` and `eTag` (quotes trimmed; an entity tag that still holds a quote is not told) absent for `marker` and for a `delete` that carries no entity tag - a delete marker removed for good, or a version whose entity tag exceeded `delivery.MaxItemETag`; `versionId` absent for the null version; `sequencer` is `Seq.String()`; no `requestParameters`, `responseElements`, `awsRegion`, `configurationId`. **The Deliverer**: `app.Notifier` (`NewNotifier(NotifierConfig{Publishers, Logger})`) is the `Deliverer` for `n:`; it asks an `app.PublisherSource` (`Publisher(ctx, target) (ports.EventPublisher, error)`, and `PublisherSourceFunc`; 8.2.5 implements it in the composition root, making a publisher a target on first use) and publishes `ports.Event{ID: item.ID(), Type: ports.MessageNotificationObject, Sequence: Seq.Index, Time: At, Data: json.RawMessage(record)}` - the adapters of 8.2.3 and 8.2.4 send `Data` as the body, and `json.Marshal(e.Data)` gives the same bytes. Every failure it returns is a `delivery.Error` whose text is its class only: a publisher's class is kept, an error without one is `internal` (tried again) or `timeout` when it wraps `context.DeadlineExceeded`, so neither an endpoint nor the words of a receiver can reach a status or a log. An item that is not an `n:` item of this target is held with `internal`, as the worker holds an item of a kind nothing delivers. An item that is not to be sent - a target of kind `s3`, a change that is not told, **a target that no longer admits the bucket** (rows appended while a document named it, left after the document was removed and the target narrowed) - is not sent and passes as `rejected`, logged at Debug by target and reason, never by key: tenants stay apart, and the target is not held for ever by rows it may not have. **Tests** (`internal/app/notify_test.go`): authorization by the built-in roles with the denial in the trail and nothing changed; a table of `Set` (kept in order, IDs and queue filled past a taken ID, a target closed to the bucket, missing, of kind s3, one of two refused, rules `Validate` refuses, no bucket, the store unavailable, a removal unavailable) with the rules before kept on refusal; the caller's rules not changed; the three refusals in the same words, naming no endpoint; the store refuses what the use case let through; an unreadable target store is not "no target"; removal by `Set` and `Delete`, twice, audited; no auditor; `Get` of later, broken, missing and absent documents; the record of every class and edge (no actor, null version, empty object, marker removed for good); `NotificationEventName` for every `delivery.Event`; `NotificationKey` cases with round trip; the golden file `internal/app/testdata/notification-records.golden.jsonl` (one record of each class); `Notifier` publishes with the item's ID, type, sequence, time and the record as body; failures keep their class, say only it, become `timeout` at the end of a deadline, ask no publisher for an item not sent, and log no key or marked URL; `FuzzNotificationRecord` (arbitrary key, actor, size, version ID, entity tag, place and kind: valid JSON of one record, no `requestParameters`, the key round-trips, `userIdentity` exactly when there is an actor, `versionId` exactly when the version is not null, no quote in `eTag`). Open, for the owner: whether passing as `rejected` the rows of a target that no longer admits their bucket is wanted, or a class of its own (a domain change); and whether `~` and `*` should be encoded as some S3 receivers expect (`QueryEscape` keeps `~`, encodes `*`; any URL decoder reads both).

##### Open questions / risks
- A webhook's 404 and 410 are classed `rejected` - passed and counted, where a receiver whose path went away loses every message (threat model, question 46)
- Rows of a target that no longer admits their bucket pass as `rejected` - or a class of their own? (8.2.1; question 47)
- The encoding of `~` and `*` in a key (`QueryEscape` keeps `~` and encodes `*`; some S3 receivers expect otherwise), and `eventTime` in nanoseconds (`RFC3339Nano`) where S3 gives milliseconds - should it be cut to milliseconds? (8.2.1)
- GET of a configuration writes both kinds of a creation or a removal as the wildcard, so a document put with `:Put` and `:CompleteMultipartUpload` reads back as `s3:ObjectCreated:*` - drift for Terraform or CloudFormation (8.2.2)
- Filter names are case-sensitive: only `prefix` and `suffix`, in lower case, as the S3 reference writes them; a client that sends `Prefix` is answered 400, where S3 may be more lenient (8.2.2)
- The record `system/outbox` is paced once a minute per node: across a change of leader two nodes may each write one within the minute (8.2.7 (3))
- `keep_firing_for` of `CactusFSDeliveryStalled` needs prometheus-operator v0.65 or later (and Prometheus 2.42 or later) for the PrometheusRule of the chart (8.2.7 review (3))
- `egress.classify` misses a TLS alert that arrives after the handshake: classed `connect`, not `tls` (question 50)
- An audit target that a receiver refuses for good stalls rather than passes the record (question 48)
- A new audit target is sent the trail from sequence 1 (question 49)
- Delete of an audit target needs only `admin:DeleteTarget` (question 51)
- The OpenAPI description of `audit` does not yet say that it needs `admin:GetAuditLog` (a contract change, with `make gen`; not made in 8.2.9, which may not change the contract)
- `networkPolicy.egressTo` is enforced only where the network plugin enforces NetworkPolicies; a target's address must be known as a range - a NetworkPolicy names no host

#### Report: 8C - replication between sites (8.1.1 to 8.1.11)
**Status:** done - 8.1.1 to 8.1.11 done, each with its gate green on linux amd64 (8.1.11: reviewed 0/2/9, all addressed; `make check` PASS on the final tree, `make test-chaos` PASS 1 387 s on the same product code)
**Branch:** a worktree of `main` (HEAD 6ed927e5 when 8.1.11 began)   **Commits:** 36 for 8.1.1 to 8.1.10 (3755c6a5..6ed927e5: 33 of the steps, 3 fixes of tests that failed a gate on the way); 8.1.11 committed after its gate, with the fixes of two tests that failed once on the way

##### What was done
- 8.1.1 and 8.1.1a - the destination: replica mode (`ReplicationService.ReplicaMode`/`SetReplicaMode`), replica requests with signed `x-cactusfs-replica-*` headers and signed payloads, the questions a source asks, `403 ObjectLocked` and `400 ReplicaHeaderNotTaken`, `x-amz-replication-status` (commits 3755c6a5, def0e531; docs b2e6a651; Decisions "8.1.1 as written", "8.1.1 review", "8.1.1a as written", "8.1.1a review")

##### Decisions made
- No change of the entry schema, of anything on disk or of the crypto design in 8C: schema 5 carried every command and field (8.0.6 to 8.0.10). One port change (`ports.SiteClient.ListParts`, `ports.SitePart.Size`; 8.1.4 review), one local domain sentinel (`domain.ErrVersioningRequired`; 8.1.3), one class (`delivery.ClassObjectLock`; 8.1.4 re-review), one contract change (the optional `ObjectMetadata.replication_status`, additive, decided by the lead session; 8.1.10) and descriptions of `admin.yaml` (8.1.7)
- The client of another site is our own, on `internal/adapters/sigv4`; no new dependency (8.1.2 (1); ADR-0026 open 3)
- `s3:ReplicateObject` and `s3:ReplicateDelete` are granted by name only - no wildcard, no bucket policy; the questions of a source are judged as `s3:ReplicateObject` and answer existence and entity tag only (8.1.1, 8.1.1a; ADR-0026)
- Codes of our own where a source must tell apart what an ordinary client need not: `403 ObjectLocked`, `400 ReplicaHeaderNotTaken` (8.1.1a (6), 8.1.1a review (3))
- Every delete says who deleted (`DeleteOptions.By`), so a lifecycle marker is never sent; visible: a notification of a delete now names who deleted (8.1.4 (2))
- Waves never hold two rows of one object at the destination; `HeadVersion` before every send; a version of parts goes on from the parts that arrived within one leader's time; the deadline of an attempt is generous, and the egress client's no-progress timeout ends a stalled transfer (8.1.4 and its reviews)
- One destination bucket a source bucket, as the use case's rule (8.1.4 review (4))
- A resync walks in the order of the version index, through the same replicator, never lifts `FAILED`, begins again without bound while its target loses rows, and is preempted by the outbox at most three times a version (8.1.6 and its review and verification)
- The status of a bucket shows the stored resync record; a held resync shows as its target's state; `CactusFSDeliveryStalled` excludes kind `s3`, which `CactusFSReplicationLag` covers (8.1.7 and its review)
- The console shows the configuration and replica mode and does not edit them; Promote asks for the bucket's name typed exactly (8.1.10 (3), (4))
- Fail-back is written down as the code does it: a replica is never sent on, also after its bucket's promotion, so a fail-back carries only what the promoted bucket wrote itself; ADR-0026 corrected and its open 18 added ("8.1.11 as written")

##### Open questions / risks
- ADR-0026 open 1 to 4 keep their defaults: active-passive, replica mode enforced by the state; version IDs the same at both sites; a client of our own; a replica bucket refuses the root identity's ordinary writes too
- ADR-0026 open 5: the root identity holds `s3:ReplicateObject` and `s3:ReplicateDelete` (threat model, question 52)
- ADR-0026 open 6: the null version of before versions (stored at sequence 0) is sent at sequence 1, as `max(seq, 1)`
- ADR-0026 open 7: a retention that ends within 15 minutes (`object.RetentionMargin`) of the source's clock is left out of a copy, and a change of such a retention is passed - the copy is unretained there for at most those minutes
- ADR-0026 open 22 (new, review of 8.1.11): the replication key can lock the replica for good - its later-change grants let it put a compliance retention of any length, or legal holds, on any version of the replica bucket and rewrite its tags, with no source header needed; should a replica bucket take later changes from that key only with the signed source header? (question 59)
- ADR-0026 open 8: a row of a bucket no longer sent to its target leaves its version `PENDING` for good (default: no status; a resync of the new configuration settles them)
- ADR-0026 open 9: two configurations naming one bucket there, put at the same moment through two nodes, may both pass the use case's check; closing it needs a schema change (question 53)
- ADR-0026 open 13: rows lost under an earlier leader do not restart a walk under way; closing it needs `Lost` in the resync record, a schema change (question 56)
- ADR-0026 open 14: a user's delete marker made before the configuration is never resynced (question 57)
- ADR-0026 open 15: a resync's restarts, preemptions and reasons to wait are in the metrics and the log, not in a bucket's status
- ADR-0026 open 17: the admin API tells the replication status of the current version only (no `version_id` on `/object/metadata`)
- ADR-0026 open 18 (new, 8.1.11): fail-back carries only what the promoted bucket wrote itself - the versions it took as a replica are never sent on, and if the old site was lost they cross only as copies with new IDs. ADR-0026 said "everything crosses again", which the code never did; the documents now say what it does. Should a promoted bucket send its replicas on - a change of the replicated format? (question 55)
- The start of a resync is audited after its commit, and a resync asked again can be overwritten in the narrow gap between the walk's read of the record and its proposal; both need a schema change (8.1.6 review (m3); ADR-0026 open 19; question 54)
- `CactusFSDeliveryStalled` no longer covers kind `s3`; `CactusFSReplicationLag` and `CactusFSReplicationResyncHeld` do - the routing of alerts must follow (8.1.7; ADR-0026 open 21; question 58)
- Whether the console should edit a bucket's replication configuration and make a bucket a replica; it shows both, as the row asked (8.1.10)
- The 8.1.9 row's "B's audit trail counts the puts" cannot hold - a copy sent again is refused and leaves no record: should it read "B's metrics count the puts, its audit trail the copies"? (8.1.9 (7))
- The notification rules' defaulted `id` (8.2.2), raised at the review of 8.1.3 (6): the contract marks `id` of a notification rule required and the use case gives one to a rule without; replication rules are held to their contract's required fields - should notification rules be too (a change of answers that are released)?
- ADR-0026 open 20: a rule of the first form silent on delete markers copies none, where S3 copies them (8.1.3 (6))
- ADR-0026 open 10 to 12, defaults kept: a later change lost at the bound is not resynced for a version that is there; a resync sends one version at a time; `sent` is a lower bound across changes of leader
- Risks: the IPv6 path of `Cluster.CutOff` and `Isolate` has not run anywhere (the harness's networks are IPv4); a version of parts starts again from its first part after a change of leader, so an object of terabytes over a poor link with leaders that change may never arrive (ADR-0026, "Consequences")

## Goal L — a session that locks, not ends, while objects are being uploaded (Albie, 2026-10-13)

"Do not time out the session while busy uploading objects; rather disable all functionality and
show a dialog box to type the user's password to enable all functionality - unless all objects
were uploaded and the session timed out: then log off from the system."

A session past its timeout whose user has an upload in flight is *locked*: the server lets it
store objects, read its own state, unlock and sign out, and answers everything else 423
`SessionLocked`. The lock is derived from the session record and an upload lease the gateways
keep in the replicated state with the commands that exist (ADR-0027): no entry schema, no record
and no file of `internal/adapters/raftmeta` changes. The S3 API is not touched; `make test-chaos`
is not owed (write path, quorum, Raft and healing are untouched).

## Goal O — bucket details that fold, and previews of objects (Albie, 2026-10-15)

"Make the bucket details panel expandable and collapsable. Add the functionality to be able to
preview known object types e.g. image file, pdf, docx, excel etc. The user must own or have
preview assigned to them." Planned with the `planner` subagent. No change of the entry schema,
the state, the on-disk format or the crypto design: a new admin action, an ownership rule in
`iam.Decide`, one admin endpoint (contract first), renderers in the console. ADR-0028.

Preview covers: PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP; PDF; DOCX; XLSX; plain text, CSV and JSON shown as text
(the first 1 MiB). It leaves out: SVG, HTML, XML and anything with script; PPTX; legacy .doc/.xls;
HEIC, TIFF, AVIF; audio and video; SSE-C objects (the console has no customer key); objects over
the preview cap. A preview is never more than a download: whoever may preview may download.

Who may preview: the caller must be allowed `s3:GetObject` (`s3:GetObjectVersion` for a named
version) on the object AND either be allowed `admin:PreviewObject` on it, or be its owner - the
user that committed the version shown (`Version.CreatedBy == "user/<name>"`). An explicit Deny of
`admin:PreviewObject` refuses the owner too; an API key's inline policy must allow both actions;
a locked session previews nothing; root may; anonymous never (no bucket policy can name an
`admin:` action). Decided by the one `ports.Authorizer`.

## Goal P — check for the latest release and upgrade from the console (Albie, 2026-11-09)

"add functionallaty to check for the latest and allow to upgrade using the webapp." Planned with
the `planner` subagent on 2026-11-09; not started (the session that planned it was given the goal
"update documentation, rebuild all binaries then commit to github" before P.0). No change of the
entry schema, the state, the on-disk format or the crypto design: nothing about releases is
replicated - what a node found is kept in its memory, and the progress of an upgrade is read from
the cluster itself. ADR-0029 (to be written in P.0); an amendment to ADR-0023 (the update client
follows redirects and reads more than 64 KiB).

Air gap (CLAUDE.md §3): nothing is asked of any server until an operator sets `update-source`
(https only); installing needs `upgrade-mode` as well. Both are off by default. What may be
installed: a release whose `SHA256SUMS` (binary) or `digests.txt` (image) carries a Sigstore
bundle that verifies offline against the embedded trusted root, for the identity of
`release.yml` at `refs/tags/v<that version>`, and that is a newer patch of the running minor or
the newest patch of the next one. Who: reading `admin:GetUpdates` (`cluster-admin`, `auditor`);
asking now `admin:CheckForUpdates` and installing `admin:UpgradeCluster` (`cluster-admin`); the
installation only from a console session whose user types the password again, judged by the server.

Facts found while planning: no release has been published yet (`git tag -l` is empty), so a check
finds nothing until a `v<version>` tag is pushed, and the Kubernetes mode needs a release made after
P.4 (signed `digests.txt`); every test uses a local mirror and a VirtualSigstore. `egress` caps
bodies at 64 KiB and follows no redirect (ADR-0023), and GitHub's asset downloads redirect. Sessions
are replicated, so the password is judged inside the upgrade request, not recorded on the session.

Windows: replaced, "restart required", no automatic restart - yes; (7) clusters of binaries on VMs:
commands only - yes; (8) trusted root embedded, refreshed each release, `update-trusted-root`
overrides - accept; (9) no HTTPS proxy - yes; (10) a ValidatingAdmissionPolicy pinning images to
`@sha256:` - residual risk, later; (11) release notes a link only - yes.

## Milestone 9 — Visual policy builder (Albie, 2026-10-13)

"Add the visual policy builder to the milestones." The console edits every policy - a
named policy (the Policies screen), a bucket's and a sub-bucket's (`SubBuckets.tsx`), an
API key's inline policy (`ApiKeys.tsx`) - as a box of JSON. This milestone gives all four
one builder made by choosing - who, what, where, when - beside the JSON it comes to. The
JSON stays the truth: it is what is sent, as shown, and the server parses, validates and
stores it as before. Whatever decides is still the one `ports.Authorizer`; the console
reckons no decision, no coverage of a wildcard and no "open to anyone" - the node answers
each (ADR-0032).

What the builder covers: everything the product parses - Version, Sid, Effect, Action
and Resource patterns, the four condition keys with their operators, a bucket policy's
Principal (users and anyone, in every form it is written), the confinements of bucket
and sub-bucket policies. What it leaves to the JSON view, kept and marked, never
dropped: layout; anything the answering node's catalogue does not list; a text it cannot
read (then it is disabled with the reason). Not in the product, so in neither view:
`NotAction`, `NotResource`, `NotPrincipal`, principals other than users and anyone,
other condition keys and operators.

Order: 9.1 ∥ 9.2 → 9.3 → 9.4 → 9.5 → 9.6 (one regeneration, on the test host) →
9.8 → 9.9; 9.7 runs beside 9.1 to 9.5; 9.10 and 9.11 beside 9.8 and 9.9 once 9.6 is
done; then 9.12 and 9.13. No step changes the Raft entry schema, the on-disk format or
the crypto design; none touches the write path, quorum, Raft or healing, so `make
test-chaos` is not a gate of this milestone (it is run in 9.13 all the same).

## Milestone 10 — One deployment script for every container platform (Albie, 2026-11-21)

Planned with the `planner` subagent on 2026-11-21. Albie's goal: "write me a deployment
script and give me the ability to deploy to all containers platform i.e. docker desktop,
docker ce, podman, k3s, k8s, rancher docker desktop ... then update the documentation,
rebuild binaries and commit code to github." Order: 10.0 to 10.13 as listed; each step
ends with `make check` green. Hosts used for acceptance are passed as variables and never
written into the repository.
